headline: Pretrained genomic sequence models are adapted to new tasks and contexts
label: Genomic Foundation Model Adaptation
summary: Recent preprints and publications report few-shot transfer of genomic language model embeddings to gene expression and CRISPR editing outcome prediction.
synthesis: The common thread is reuse of pretrained or sequence-to-function models under limited task-specific data. xDecoder decodes genomic language model and S2F embeddings to predict personal gene expression, with few-shot performance reported. inDecay applies a parameter-efficient, cell-type-aware few-shot model to CRISPR-induced indel proportions, transferring from cell lines to zygotes. CENO proposes 300M to 1B parameter long-context autoregressive genomic world models, built on Mamba, sparse attention, and mixture-of-experts backbones, and evaluated for variant effect prediction and regulatory design. A review of sequence-to-function deep learning addresses interpretability and failure modes, and a primate cerebellum study applies sequence-based deep learning to transposable element subfamilies. What is new here is explicit cell-type conditioning and parameter-efficient few-shot transfer across biological contexts. The scDiffusion sampling modification and the bpAI-TAC resolution model are methodologically adjacent rather than part of this thread.
